To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the risk of post-transplantation malignancy is related to individual predisposition, pretransplantation disease, viral status, and intensity of immunotherapy; (ii) CMV remains a significant cause of infection in the mid-to late period after transplantation; (iii) procurement and preservation injury is a rare cause of early allograft dysfunction; and (iv) hepatic artery thrombus and biliary stricture remain significant causes of early post-transplantation morbidity.

the most common complications of liver transplantation are infections, surgical complications, and malignancies, and that the risk of such complications is cumulative and increases with time after transplantation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most significant cause of morbidity and mortality in the early period after liver transplantation is surgical complications, whereas in the mid- to late period, infections, particularly CMV infection, and development of malignancies become more common causes of morbidity and death.
complications of liver transplantation are common and are not limited to immunologic injury, but include surgical, infectious, and oncologic complications.

post-liver transplantation complications are not limited to the immune-mediated complications of acute and chronic rejection and recurrence of original diseases but also include surgical complications, infections and development of de-novo malignancies.
